subject.title: Durable Core PR 6/6: add read-only durable inspection

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a core, opt-in durable-runtime layer—with persisted cross-owner coordination state, recovery behavior, and public Gateway/CLI inspection—or keep these concerns within existing owner-specific systems?
rationale: This decision determines whether the new state model and public API should exist at all; it cannot be resolved by a mechanical code repair or by the contributor’s proof alone.

options.title: Pause pending RFC direction
options.body: Keep this cumulative PR series open for discussion and require an explicit maintainer decision on the residual durable-core boundary before reviewing it as landable code.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core contract
options.body: Accept only a clearly scoped residual contract, then request a current-main-rebased implementation and upgrade proof for the accepted surface.

options.title: Keep durability owner-specific
options.body: Reject the shared core layer and route any demonstrated gaps to the existing task, flow, subagent, session, and delivery owners.

recommendation.title: Pause pending RFC direction
recommendation.body: Keep this cumulative PR series open for discussion and require an explicit maintainer decision on the residual durable-core boundary before reviewing it as landable code.

likelyOwner.reason: A cross-cutting core state and protocol contract needs product-level ownership beyond the contributor’s implementation context.
